subject.title: Feature request: Read pinned Telegram messages via bot API

question: Should OpenClaw expose Telegram pinned-message reads now, and should the first version be an explicit on-demand gated action/command rather than automatic session context injection?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the feature changes Telegram data-access scope and session-context behavior, so automation should not choose the default or permission model without maintainer intent.

options.title: Ship on-demand gated read first
options.body: Add a Telegram-owned list-pins or read-pinned action/command backed by getChat.pinned_message with an explicit config/action gate and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Fold into broader Telegram read work
options.body: Treat this as part of #12756 so pinned reads, message history reads, and permission semantics are designed together.

options.title: Defer automatic context injection
options.body: Keep automatic session-start pinned context out of scope until maintainers approve storage, context-injection, and privacy defaults.

recommendation.title: Ship on-demand gated read first
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram-owned list-pins or read-pinned action/command backed by getChat.pinned_message with an explicit config/action gate and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining blocker is the Telegram product/security policy choice surfaced by prior maintainer routing rather than a code ownership dispute.
